payload.summary: D1 (narration-stutter, product=delegated): critical events become ENGINE-VOICED ONLY — the narrator is never asked to narrate them, rather than narrating them alongside the engine. Rationale: the epic-review guarantee (deduction-bearing facts must reach the player in the engine's exact words) is preserved absolutely and more cheaply — no text comparison, no reliance on the model producing a differing string; the stutter disappears because the fact is stated once; and the prompt shrinks to scenery only, cutting tokens. Cost: critical moments read plainer, which is the correct trade where precision beats flavour. Consequence: NarrationLine.source must distinguish deliberate engine voice ('engine') from vendor failure ('fallback'), or the offline-notice misfires on every critical event.
